preamble: The retroflex sibilant [ʂ] merges into the alveolo-palatal [ɕ]: the tongue tip lowers, and the blade of the tongue moves to the palate.

examples.note: Sanskrit ṣ and s both appear as ś in Māgadhī, where Sanskrit's three sibilants merged into one. The form is the textbook Māgadhī one (r also becomes l); it was not checked against a primary text.

sources: Pischel, R. (1900). Grammatik der Prakrit-Sprachen. Trübner.
Masica, C. P. (1991). The Indo-Aryan Languages. Cambridge University Press.
